tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

1	"""Execute the preparation, training and export stages described by a run file.
2	The workflow prepares model and data artifacts, records their identities and tracks
3	attempts so recovery can reuse compatible outputs and reject changed inputs. GPU
4	runtime parsing and training are deferred until execution, keeping the same run
5	specification usable for planning and submission on a CPU-only machine.
6	"""
7	
8	import asyncio
9	import copy
10	import fcntl
11	import hashlib
12	import importlib
13	import json
14	import os
15	import shutil
16	import sys
17	import time
18	import uuid
19	from contextlib import contextmanager
20	from pathlib import Path
21	from types import SimpleNamespace
22	
23	from open_instruct import logger_utils
24	from open_instruct.miles.configuration import advisories, inference_profiles, topology
25	from open_instruct.miles.errors import InputError
26	from open_instruct.miles.evaluation import evaluation
27	from open_instruct.miles.execution.timing import stage
28	from open_instruct.miles.infrastructure import artifacts
29	from open_instruct.miles.rewards import judging
30	
31	logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)
32	
33	
34	def write_json(path, document):
35	    artifacts.atomic_json(Path(path), document)
36	
37	
38	def fingerprint(document):
39	    # OPD checkpoint retention is operational, and its empty native override
40	    # table was historically optional. Preserve that run identity on resume.
41	    if isinstance(document, dict) and document.get("training", {}).get("algorithm") == "opd":
42	        document = {key: value for key, value in document.items() if not (key == "miles" and value == {})}
43	        document["training"] = {key: value for key, value in document["training"].items() if key != "keep_checkpoints"}
44	    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
45	
46	
47	COMPILER_CACHE_CORE_KEYS = (
48	    "compiler_cache",
49	    "compiler_cache_root",
50	    "compiler_cache_restore",
51	    "compiler_cache_diagnostics",
52	    "compiler_cache_tilelang",
53	    "compiler_cache_max_storage_bytes",
54	    "compiler_cache_publish_interval_seconds",
55	)
56	
57	
58	def recovery_configuration_matches(root, previous, document):
59	    """Allow operational recovery, cache, and artifact-cadence changes on resume.
60	
61	    Authenticate the recorded full specification before normalizing it, including
62	    older runs that hashed auto_resume or predate the explicit host-memory field.
63	    """
64	    if previous["spec_sha256"] == fingerprint(document):
65	        return True
66	    path = Path(root) / "run-spec.json"
67	    if not path.is_file():
68	        return False
69	    recorded = json.loads(path.read_text())
70	    if fingerprint(recorded) != previous["spec_sha256"]:
71	        return False
72	    if "memory" in document["launch"]:
73	        # Launchers requested this amount before it became a configurable field.
74	        # Do not use current loader defaults: this authenticates the historical
75	        # resource commitment even if future launch defaults change.
76	        # Preserve explicit saved values so actual resource changes still fail.
77	        recorded.setdefault("launch", {}).setdefault("memory", "256 GiB")
78	    for key in ("auto_resume", "max_retries"):
79	        if key in document["launch"]:
80	            recorded.setdefault("launch", {})[key] = document["launch"][key]
81	    # Compiler-cache persistence is an optimization (a miss compiles locally), so a
82	    # resumed run may move or disable its cache, e.g. when the shared root is full.
83	    adopt_keys(recorded, document, ("compiler_cache",))
84	    if isinstance(recorded.get("core"), dict) and isinstance(document.get("core"), dict):
85	        adopt_keys(recorded["core"], document["core"], COMPILER_CACHE_CORE_KEYS)
86	    # Checkpoint/evaluation cadence changes only future artifact production.
87	    # Keep training horizon, evaluation tasks/scorers, and all recipe fields strict.
88	    if isinstance(recorded.get("training"), dict) and isinstance(document.get("training"), dict):
89	        adopt_keys(recorded["training"], document["training"], ("save_interval",))
90	    if isinstance(recorded.get("evaluation"), dict) and isinstance(document.get("evaluation"), dict):
91	        adopt_keys(recorded["evaluation"], document["evaluation"], ("interval",))
92	        old_tasks = recorded["evaluation"].get("tasks", [])
93	        new_tasks = document["evaluation"].get("tasks", [])
94	        if len(old_tasks) == len(new_tasks):
95	            for old_task, new_task in zip(old_tasks, new_tasks):
96	                adopt_keys(old_task, new_task, ("interval",))
97	    return recorded == document
98	
99	
100	def adopt_keys(recorded, document, keys):
101	    for key in keys:
102	        recorded.pop(key, None)
103	        if key in document:
104	            recorded[key] = document[key]
105	
106	
107	def record_attempt(root, limit):
108	    """Append this start to the run's attempt ledger, refusing once the cap is reached.
109	
110	    Beaker restarts a preempted task without limit, so a run that is preempted before it
111	    can save advances nothing and restarts forever. Each restart is a fresh process with
112	    no memory of the last, so the ledger on the shared filesystem is the only thing that
113	    can count them.
114	
115	    `limit` counts *retries*, so the first start is never refused and -1 disables the cap.
116	    It counts every restart, including ones that made progress; a cap on unproductive
117	    restarts alone would need the checkpoint state, which is not resolved this early.
118	    """
119	    path = Path(root) / "attempts.json"
120	    attempts = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.is_file() else []
121	    if limit >= 0 and len(attempts) > limit:
122	        raise InputError(
123	            f"Run reached launch.max_retries={limit} after {len(attempts)} starts: {root}. "
124	            "Raise launch.max_retries to allow more, or choose a new output.root."
125	        )
126	    attempts.append(dict(attempt=len(attempts), started_unix=time.time()))
127	    write_json(path, attempts)
128	    return attempts
129	
130	
131	def model_identity(source):
132	    """Record checkpoint metadata and shard identity without hashing tens of GB."""
133	    source = Path(source)
134	    if not source.is_dir():
135	        raise InputError(
136	            f"Model directory does not exist: {source}. Check model.source and its mount in launch.weka_mounts."
137	        )
138	    files = []
139	    for path in sorted(source.rglob("*")):
140	        if not path.is_file() or path.name == "workflow-model.json":
141	            continue
142	        stat = path.stat()
143	        item = dict(path=str(path.relative_to(source)), size=stat.st_size, mtime_ns=stat.st_mtime_ns)
144	        if path.suffix in (".json", ".jinja") or path.name == ".metadata":
145	            item["sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
146	        files.append(item)
147	    if not files:
148	        raise InputError(f"Empty model directory: {source}")
149	    return dict(path=str(source), files=files)
150	
151	
152	def prepare_model(spec):
153	    source = Path(spec.model["source"])
154	    target = Path(spec.conversion["hf_output"])
155	    if source.resolve() == target.resolve() or source.resolve() in target.resolve().parents:
156	        raise InputError("Prepared model output must not be inside its read-only source")
157	    template = spec.model.get("hf_template")
158	    identity = dict(source=model_identity(source), format=spec.model["format"], conversion=spec.conversion)
159	    if template:
160	        template_path = Path(template)
161	        if not template_path.exists():
162	            raise InputError(
163	                f"model.hf_template not found: {template}. Check the path and the job's WEKA mounts; "
164	                "omit hf_template to use the checkpoint's own tokenizer and chat template."
165	            )
166	        if template_path.is_dir():
167	            if not any((template_path / name).is_file() for name in ("tokenizer.json", "tokenizer_config.json")):
168	                raise InputError(
169	                    f"model.hf_template directory has no tokenizer assets (tokenizer.json or tokenizer_config.json): "
170	                    f"{template}"
171	                )
172	        elif template_path.suffix != ".jinja":
173	            raise InputError(f"model.hf_template must be a tokenizer directory or a .jinja chat template: {template}")
174	        identity["template"] = (
175	            model_identity(template)
176	            if Path(template).is_dir()
177	            else {"path": template, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(template).read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
178	        )
179	    marker = target / "workflow-model.json"
180	    if marker.exists():
181	        recorded = json.loads(marker.read_text())
182	        if recorded["identity"] != identity:
183	            raise InputError("Prepared model identity changed; choose a new output.root")
184	        if recorded.get("prepared_files") != model_identity(target)["files"]:
185	            raise InputError("Prepared model files changed or lack an integrity inventory")
186	        return str(target)
187	    if target.exists():
188	        raise InputError(
189	            f"Refusing to adopt an incomplete or unrelated prepared model: {target}. Choose a new output.root."
190	        )
191	    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
192	    staging = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.preparing-{uuid.uuid4().hex}")
193	    staging.mkdir()
194	    try:
195	        if spec.model["format"] == "hf":
196	            if not (source / "config.json").is_file() or not list(source.glob("*.safetensors")):
197	                raise InputError(f"Expected an HF config and safetensors weights in {source}")
198	            for path in source.iterdir():
199	                if path.name == "workflow-model.json":
200	                    continue
201	                destination = staging / path.name
202	                if path.is_file() and path.suffix == ".safetensors":
203	                    destination.symlink_to(path.resolve())
204	                elif path.is_dir():
205	                    shutil.copytree(path, destination, symlinks=False)
206	                else:
207	                    # Tokenizer.save_pretrained overwrites these files. Never
208	                    # allow those writes to follow a link into the source.
209	                    shutil.copy2(path, destination)
210	        else:
211	            _convert_native(spec, staging)
212	        if template:
213	            template_path = Path(template)
214	            if template_path.is_dir():
215	                tokenizer_utils = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.tokenizer_utils")
216	                tokenizer = tokenizer_utils.load_tokenizer(template_path, trust_remote_code=True)
217	                # A stale standalone template overrides tokenizer_config in
218	                # Transformers. Remove only our copied templates before saving.
219	                (staging / "chat_template.jinja").unlink(missing_ok=True)
220	                if (staging / "chat_templates").exists():
221	                    shutil.rmtree(staging / "chat_templates")
222	                tokenizer.save_pretrained(staging)
223	                # Stop-token ids belong with the template (Olmo 3.5 ends answers
224	                # with eos but tool calls with <|im_end|>); carry them along.
225	                if (template_path / "generation_config.json").is_file():
226	                    shutil.copyfile(template_path / "generation_config.json", staging / "generation_config.json")
227	                rendered = tokenizer.chat_template or ""
228	            else:
229	                shutil.copyfile(template_path, staging / "chat_template.jinja")
230	                rendered = template_path.read_text()
231	            for placeholder in ("[CUTOFF_DATE]",):
232	                if placeholder in rendered:
233	                    logger.warning(
234	                        "Chat template %s contains the literal placeholder %s; every prompt will render it verbatim",
235	                        template_path,
236	                        placeholder,
237	                    )
238	        if model_identity(source) != identity["source"]:
239	            raise InputError("Source model changed during preparation")
240	        write_json(staging / marker.name, {"identity": identity, "prepared_files": model_identity(staging)["files"]})
241	        staging.rename(target)
242	    except BaseException:
243	        # Retain a failed conversion for inspection; never present it as complete.
244	        raise
245	    return str(target)
246	
247	
248	def _convert_native(spec, target):
249	    converter = importlib.import_module("olmo_core.nn.hf.convert_checkpoint")
250	    core_config = importlib.import_module("olmo_core.config")
251	    torch = importlib.import_module("torch")
252	    saved = converter.load_config(spec.model["source"])
253	    if not saved or "model" not in saved or "dataset" not in saved:
254	        raise InputError("Native input must include its saved model and tokenizer configuration")
255	    converter.convert_checkpoint_to_hf(
256	        spec.model["source"],
257	        target,
258	        copy.deepcopy(saved["model"]),
259	        copy.deepcopy(saved["dataset"]["tokenizer"]),
260	        dtype=core_config.DType(spec.conversion.get("dtype", "bfloat16")),
261	        max_sequence_length=spec.compile().core.max_sequence_length,
262	        device=torch.device(spec.conversion.get("device", "cpu")),
263	        validate=False,
264	    )
265	
266	
267	def parse_runtime(config):
268	    try:
269	        native = importlib.import_module("miles.utils.arguments")
270	    except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
271	        if error.name not in {"miles", "miles.utils", "miles.utils.arguments"}:
272	            raise
273	        raise InputError(
274	            "MILES is not installed in this environment. Use plan for local config checks; validate/train require the pinned MILES/Core runtime image."
275	        ) from error
276	    original = sys.argv
277	    try:
278	        sys.argv = [original[0], *config.arguments()]
279	        args = native.parse_args()
280	    finally:
281	        sys.argv = original
282	    if args.train_backend != "olmo_core":
283	        raise InputError(
284	            "This MILES installation does not select the olmo_core backend; use the pinned MILES/Core runtime image built by scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh --miles."
285	        )
286	    if args.load:
287	        checkpoint = importlib.import_module("miles.backends.core_utils.checkpoint")
288	        _, manifest = checkpoint.resume_manifest(args.load)
289	        args.start_rollout_id = manifest["clock"]["next_rollout_id"]
290	    return args
291	
292	
293	def train_config(config, *, export_hf=None, background_evaluation=None):
294	    with stage(SimpleNamespace(save=config.miles.get("save")), "runtime_argument_parsing"):
295	        args = parse_runtime(config)
296	    args.background_evaluation = background_evaluation
297	    args.core_evaluation_snapshot = (
298	        "open_instruct.miles.evaluation.evaluation.training_snapshot" if background_evaluation else None
299	    )
300	    os.environ.setdefault("SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE", "olmo_sglang.models")
301	    with stage(args, "driver_module_import"):
302	        driver = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.execution.driver")
303	    return asyncio.run(driver.train(args, export_hf=export_hf))
304	
305	
306	@contextmanager
307	def run_directory(spec):
308	    root = Path(spec.output["root"])
309	    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
310	    with (root / ".workflow.lock").open("a") as stream:
311	        try:
312	            fcntl.flock(stream.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
313	        except BlockingIOError as error:
314	            raise InputError(
315	                f"Another process owns this run: {root}. Wait for it to finish or choose a different output.root. "
316	                "If the previous node disappeared, check the previous attempt and shared-filesystem lock "
317	                "recovery before retrying; ownership may not yet have been released. "
318	                "Do not delete the lock file to bypass an active or recovering lock."
319	            ) from error
320	        document = spec.to_dict()
321	        identity = fingerprint(document)
322	        path = root / "workflow.json"
323	        if path.exists():
324	            previous = json.loads(path.read_text())
325	            if not recovery_configuration_matches(root, previous, document):
326	                raise InputError("Run configuration changed; choose a new output.root")
327	            if previous["status"] == "complete":
328	                raise InputError(f"Run already completed: {root}. Choose a new output.root for another run.")
329	            if not spec.launch["auto_resume"]:
330	                raise InputError(
331	                    f"Run already exists and launch.auto_resume is false: {root}. "
332	                    "Set launch.auto_resume=true to resume, or choose a new output.root."
333	                )
334	        # Runs recorded before this field existed carry no cap, and resuming one must not
335	        # depend on the field being present in the older specification.
336	        attempts = record_attempt(root, spec.launch.get("max_retries", -1))
337	        state = dict(spec_sha256=identity, status="preparing", started_unix=time.time(), attempt=len(attempts) - 1)
338	        write_json(root / "run-spec.json", document)
339	        write_json(root / "plan.json", spec.plan())
340	        write_json(path, state)
341	        try:
342	            yield root, state
343	        except BaseException as error:
344	            state.update(status="failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}", finished_unix=time.time())
345	            write_json(path, state)
346	            raise
347	
348	
349	def execute(spec):
350	    with run_directory(spec) as (root, state):
351	        timing_args = SimpleNamespace(save=root)
352	        with stage(timing_args, "model_preparation"):
353	            hf = prepare_model(spec)
354	        with stage(timing_args, "data_module_import"):
355	            data = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.datasets.run_data")
356	        planned = spec.compile({"hf_checkpoint": hf})
357	        with stage(timing_args, "data_preparation"):
358	            prepared = data.prepare_data(
359	                spec.data,
360	                Path(hf),
361	                root / "prepared" / "data",
362	                max_prompt_length=planned.miles.get("rollout_max_prompt_len", 2048),
363	                seed=planned.miles.get("seed", 17),
364	                registry_overrides={
365	                    name: {
366	                        "factory": "open_instruct.miles.rewards.judge_registry.NamedJudgeVerifier",
367	                        "config": {"name": name},
368	                    }
369	                    for name in spec.judges["judging"]["bindings"]
370	                },
371	            )
372	        registry_module = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.rewards.judge_registry")
373	        resolved = judging.registry(spec.judges)
374	        if spec.judges["judging"]["bindings"]:
375	            resolved = registry_module.registry()
376	            if resolved is None:
377	                raise InputError("Named judges require the managed launcher (or a resolved registry)")
378	        registry_module.validate_data(prepared, resolved)
379	        config = spec.compile({**prepared, "hf_checkpoint": hf})
380	        profile = getattr(config, "inference_profile", None)
381	        inventory_root = os.environ.get("OI_MILES_INFERENCE_REPORT_DIR")
382	        if profile and profile.get("selected") in inference_profiles.PROFILES:
383	            layout = topology.plan(spec, config)
384	            if inventory_root:
385	                hardware = inference_profiles.check_cluster_hardware(profile, inventory_root, layout)
386	            elif layout["replicas"] == 1:
387	                hardware = inference_profiles.check_hardware(profile, node=layout["nodes"][0])
388	            else:
389	                raise InputError(
390	                    "A matched multi-node inference profile requires per-replica GPU inventories; "
391	                    "use the managed cluster launcher instead of direct train."
392	                )
393	        else:
394	            hardware = []
395	        write_json(root / "inference-profile.json", {"profile": profile, "hardware": hardware})
396	        checkpoint_root = Path(config.miles["save"])
397	        if spec.launch["auto_resume"] and (checkpoint_root / "core-latest.json").exists():
398	            config.miles["load"] = str(checkpoint_root)
399	        resolved_plan = config.plan()
400	        write_json(root / "resolved-plan.json", resolved_plan)
401	        advisories.emit(resolved_plan)
402	        state.update(status="training", training_started_unix=time.time())
403	        write_json(root / "workflow.json", state)
404	        result = train_config(
405	            config,
406	            export_hf=spec.output["hf_dir"] if spec.output["export_hf"] else None,
407	            **(
408	                {"background_evaluation": evaluation.runtime(spec, config.miles)}
409	                if spec.evaluation["mode"] == "background"
410	                else {}
411	            ),
412	        )
413	        # A deliberate debug exit is successful execution, not a completed run.
414	        completed = result.get("completed_rollout_ids") if result else None
415	        complete = (
416	            completed is None
417	            or bool(result.get("pools_exhausted"))
418	            or (bool(result.get("stopped_for_time")) and not result.get("time_stop_resumable"))
419	            or (
420	                (completed[-1] + 1 if completed else result["start_rollout_id"])
421	                == result.get("num_rollout", config.miles.get("num_rollout"))
422	            )
423	        )
424	        state.update(status="complete" if complete else "stopped", finished_unix=time.time(), result=result)
425	        write_json(root / "workflow.json", state)

62	    older runs that hashed auto_resume or predate the explicit host-memory field.
63	    """

75	        # resource commitment even if future launch defaults change.
76	        # Preserve explicit saved values so actual resource changes still fail.
77	        recorded.setdefault("launch", {}).setdefault("memory", "256 GiB")

116	    It counts every restart, including ones that made progress; a cap on unproductive
117	    restarts alone would need the checkpoint state, which is not resolved this early.

"""Coordinate rollout collection, Core optimizer updates and policy publication for
one training attempt. The driver connects MILES actors to Open Instruct rewards,
records and evaluation, and places checkpoint and shutdown boundaries around work
that must be recoverable. It supports barrier, refresh and engine-drain publication
while leaving model execution and weight transport to the pinned runtime.
"""

import os
import time
from functools import partial
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import ray
import wandb
from miles.backends.core_utils.publication.rolling_publication import RollingPublication
from miles.backends.core_utils.rollout import errors as rollout_errors
from miles.backends.core_utils.rollout import prepared_batch
from miles.ray import placement_group, wiring
from miles.ray.rollout.eval_dispatch import EvalDispatcher
from miles.utils import object_store
from miles.utils.compiler_cache import startup_cache
from miles.utils.data import remove_rollout_data_refs
from miles.utils.hf_utils.config import HF_EXPORT_COMPLETE_MARKER
from miles.utils.misc import should_run_periodic_action
from miles.utils.tracking_utils.tracking import define_step_key_metric_group, finish_tracking, init_tracking, log

from open_instruct import logger_utils
from open_instruct.miles.configuration import throughput
from open_instruct.miles.evaluation import evaluation as background_eval
from open_instruct.miles.execution import serving, startup
from open_instruct.miles.execution.timing import evaluation_stage, stage
from open_instruct.miles.infrastructure import infra_timeouts
from open_instruct.miles.rollout import pool_metrics

logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)


async def train(args, *, export_hf=None):
    if getattr(args, "cluster_backend", "ray") != "ray":
        raise ValueError("Core currently requires the Ray cluster backend")
    pooled = getattr(args.olmo_core, "prompt_provider", "shuffle") == "pools"
    exhaustion_type = None
    if pooled:
        exhaustion_type = getattr(rollout_errors, "PromptPoolExhausted", None)
        supported = getattr(rollout_errors, "FINITE_POOL_PROVIDERS", ())
        if (
            exhaustion_type is None
            or args.olmo_core.prompt_provider not in supported
            or not getattr(rollout_errors, "EXPLICIT_DISCARD_FEEDBACK", False)
        ):
            raise RuntimeError("Named pools require the companion MILES runtime with trained-exposure callbacks")
    budget = getattr(args.olmo_core, "max_run_seconds", None)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + budget if budget is not None else None
    # A time stop saves and leaves the run open, like a debug exit: no final export
    # or final evaluation at the stopped update. max_run_final, or no save path,
    # makes it final.
    resumable = not getattr(args.olmo_core, "max_run_final", False) and bool(getattr(args, "save", None))
    stopped_for_time = final_stop = exhausted = False
    for warning in throughput.report(vars(args), args.olmo_core)["warnings"]:
        logger.warning("Throughput [%s]: %s", warning["code"], warning["message"])
    with stage(args, "startup_cache_prepare"):
        startup_cache.prepare(args, application_root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3])
    worker_manager = None
    manager = None
    inference = None
    learner = None
    rollouts_per_epoch = None
    failure = None
    completed = []
    last_saved_rollout = args.start_rollout_id - 1 if getattr(args, "load", None) else None
    rolling = None
    refresh = args.olmo_core.publication_mode == "refresh"
    overlap = prepared_batch.enabled(args)
    prefetched = False
    logger.info(
        "Prepared-batch overlap enabled: %s; %s",
        overlap,
        "eligible" if overlap else prepared_batch.disabled_reason(args),

34	def write(path, value):
35	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
36	    temporary = path.with_name(path.name + "." + uuid.uuid4().hex + ".tmp")
37	    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, allow_nan=False))

45	def free_ports(count):
46	    """Select distinct local ports together, then release them for service startup.
47	
48	    Holding every socket until selection finishes prevents duplicates within this
49	    batch. Other processes can still claim a port after these sockets close.
50	    """
51	    ports = []
52	    with contextlib.ExitStack() as sockets:
53	        for _ in range(count):
54	            stream = sockets.enter_context(socket.socket())
55	            stream.bind(("0.0.0.0", 0))
56	            ports.append(stream.getsockname()[1])
57	    return ports

60	def terminate(process):
61	    if process is None:
62	        return
63	    # Even a finished group leader may have surviving grandchildren.
64	    with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
65	        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
66	    with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
67	        process.wait(timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(15))
68	    with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
69	        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
70	    process.wait(timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(15))

73	def require_layout(nodes, expected):
74	    live = [node for node in nodes if node.get("Alive")]
75	    actual = {node["NodeManagerAddress"]: node.get("Resources", {}).get("GPU", 0) for node in live}
76	    if len(live) != len(actual) or actual != expected:
77	        raise RuntimeError(f"Ray ownership differs from planned per-node GPU pools: {actual} != {expected}")

80	class Supervisor:
81	    def __init__(self, spec, root, rank, count):
82	        self.spec, self.root, self.rank, self.count = spec, root, rank, count
83	        self.startup_timeout = infra_timeouts.seconds(spec.launch["coordination"]["startup_timeout"])
84	        # Rendezvous has established a fresh attempt. Rank zero publishes one
85	        # budget for all subsequent startup work, including inventory/launch.
86	        deadline = time.time() + self.startup_timeout
87	        if rank == 0:
88	            write(root / "startup.json", {"deadline_unix": deadline})
89	        while not (root / "startup.json").is_file():
90	            if time.time() >= deadline:
91	                raise TimeoutError("Replica zero did not publish the startup deadline")
92	            time.sleep(1)
93	        self.startup_deadline = startup.deadline(root)
94	        self.heartbeat_timeout = infra_timeouts.seconds(spec.launch["coordination"]["heartbeat_timeout"])
95	        self.heartbeat_warning_at = {}
96	        self.children = []
97	        self.startup_tasks = []
98	        self.pending_health = {}
99	        self.logs = []
100	        self.health = {}
101	        self.health_failures = {}
102	        self.peer_heartbeats = {}
103	        self.next_health = 0.0
104	        self.log_offsets = {}
105	        self.stopping = threading.Event()
106	        self.failed = None
107	        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.heartbeat, daemon=True)
108	
109	    def heartbeat(self):
110	        while not self.stopping.is_set():
111	            try:
112	                write(self.root / f"heartbeat-{self.rank}.json", {"time": time.time(), "rank": self.rank})
113	                self.check_peer_heartbeats()
114	                for _, process in self.children:
115	                    if not (self.root / "complete.json").exists() and process.poll() is not None:
116	                        raise RuntimeError(f"Managed process {process.args[:3]} exited with {process.returncode}")
117	                if not (self.root / "complete.json").exists() and time.monotonic() >= self.next_health:
118	                    self.probe_health()
119	                    self.next_health = time.monotonic() + (2 if self.pending_health else 10)
120	            except BaseException as error:
121	                self.failed = error
122	                return
123	            self.stopping.wait(2)
124	
125	    def check_peer_heartbeats(self):
126	        now = time.time()
127	        for rank in range(self.count):
128	            # A missing directory entry during shared-filesystem publication is
129	            # not evidence that an already joined peer never rendezvoused.
130	            # Retain its last observed heartbeat, without extending its deadline.
131	            try:
132	                observed = read(self.root / f"heartbeat-{rank}.json")["time"]
133	            except FileNotFoundError:
134	                observed = self.peer_heartbeats.get(rank)
135	            else:
136	                self.peer_heartbeats[rank] = observed
137	            if observed is None:
138	                if now >= self.startup_deadline:
139	                    raise TimeoutError(f"Replica {rank} did not rendezvous")
140	            else:
141	                age = now - observed
142	                if age > min(
143	                    30, self.spec.launch["coordination"]["heartbeat_timeout"]
144	                ) and now >= self.heartbeat_warning_at.get(rank, 0):
145	                    infra_timeouts.logger.warning(
146	                        "Replica heartbeat stale: observer=%s replica=%s age_s=%.1f deadline_s=%s",
147	                        self.rank,
148	                        rank,
149	                        age,
150	                        self.heartbeat_timeout,
151	                    )
152	                    self.heartbeat_warning_at[rank] = now + 30
153	                if age > self.heartbeat_timeout:
154	                    raise RuntimeError(f"Replica {rank} heartbeat expired")
155	
156	    def probe_health(self):
157	        # Judges load on their own GPUs while Ray and the workflow start. Only
158	        # promote a service into steady-state liveness checks once HTTP is ready.
159	        for name, url in tuple(self.pending_health.items()):
160	            try:
161	                with request.urlopen(url, timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(3)) as response:
162	                    if response.status != 200:
163	                        raise OSError(f"Judge HTTP status {response.status}")
164	            except OSError as error:
165	                if time.time() >= self.startup_deadline:
166	                    raise TimeoutError(f"Judge {name} did not become ready before the startup deadline") from error
167	                continue
168	            self.health[name] = url
169	            self.pending_health.pop(name)
170	            write(self.root / f"judge-ready-{name}.json", {"ready_unix": time.time()})
171	        for name, url in tuple(self.health.items()):
172	            try:
173	                with request.urlopen(url, timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(5)) as response:
174	                    if response.status != 200:
175	                        raise RuntimeError("Unhealthy HTTP response")
176	                self.health_failures[name] = 0
177	            except (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
178	                self.health_failures[name] = self.health_failures.get(name, 0) + 1
179	                write(
180	                    self.root / f"judge-health-{self.rank}.json",
181	                    {"failures": self.health_failures, "error": str(error)},
182	                )
183	                if self.health_failures[name] >= 3:
184	                    raise RuntimeError(f"Judge {name}: three consecutive liveness failures") from error
185	
186	    def relay_logs(self):
187	        for stream in self.logs:
188	            with Path(stream.name).open("rb") as reader:
189	                reader.seek(self.log_offsets.get(stream.name, 0))
190	                raw = reader.read(16384)
191	                self.log_offsets[stream.name] = reader.tell()
192	            if raw:
193	                print(f"[{Path(stream.name).name}] " + raw.decode(errors="replace"), end="", flush=True)
194	
195	    def check(self):
196	        self.relay_logs()
197	        if self.failed:
198	            raise self.failed
199	        for label, process in self.startup_tasks:
200	            if process.poll() not in (None, 0):
201	                raise RuntimeError(f"Startup task {label} exited with {process.returncode}; see {self.root}")
202	        failures = list(self.root.glob("failed-*.json"))
203	        if failures:
204	            raise RuntimeError(f"Peer failure: {read(failures[0])}")
205	
206	    def wait(self, predicate, *, timeout=None):
207	        # Explicit timeouts are for post-training completion, which must not
208	        # inherit an already expired startup deadline.
209	        deadline = self.startup_deadline if timeout is None else time.time() + infra_timeouts.seconds(timeout)
210	        started = time.monotonic()
211	        next_warning = started + 30
212	        while True:
213	            if time.monotonic() >= next_warning:
214	                infra_timeouts.logger.warning(
215	                    "Cluster readiness still waiting: replica=%s elapsed_s=%.1f remaining_s=%.1f",
216	                    self.rank,
217	                    time.monotonic() - started,
218	                    max(0, deadline - time.time()),
219	                )
220	                next_warning = time.monotonic() + 30
221	            self.check()
222	            result = predicate()
223	            if result:
224	                return result
225	            if time.time() >= deadline:
226	                raise TimeoutError("Cluster startup/readiness deadline expired")
227	            time.sleep(1)

229	    def start(self, label, command, env, *, monitor=True):
230	        log = (self.root / f"{label}-{self.rank}.log").open("w")
231	        self.logs.append(log)
232	        process = subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True)
233	        try:
234	            write(self.root / f"process-{label}-{self.rank}.json", {"started_unix": time.time(), "pid": process.pid})
235	        except BaseException:
236	            terminate(process)
237	            raise
238	        if monitor:
239	            self.children.append((label, process))
240	        return process
241	
242	    def start_task(self, label, command, env):
243	        """Own a finite startup subprocess without treating success as a crash."""
244	        process = self.start(label, command, env, monitor=False)
245	        self.startup_tasks.append((label, process))
246	        return process
247	
248	    def run_child(self, label, command, env):
249	        process = self.start(label, command, env, monitor=False)
250	        try:
251	            while process.poll() is None:
252	                self.check()
253	                time.sleep(1)
254	            if process.returncode:
255	                raise RuntimeError(
256	                    f"{label} exited with {process.returncode}; see {self.root}/{label}-{self.rank}.log"
257	                )
258	        finally:
259	            terminate(process)
260	
261	    def close(self):
262	        self.stopping.set()
263	        self.thread.join(timeout=5)
264	        for _, process in reversed(self.children + self.startup_tasks):
265	            terminate(process)
266	        for stream in self.logs:
267	            stream.close()

414	def start_workflow(path, supervisor, env, assignments, registry):
415	    """Start preparation immediately, with separate Ray and judge readiness gates."""
416	    root, rank = supervisor.root, supervisor.rank
417	    # Endpoint discovery is complete; readiness is deliberately separate.
418	    # The driver can prepare model/data while Ray and judges initialize.
419	    write(root / "expected-ray.json", {ip: n["ray_gpus"] for ip, n in assignments.items()})
420	    write(root / "registry.json", registry)
421	    env[startup.REPORT_DIR_ENV] = str(root)
422	    for label, option in (("ray-readiness", "--probe"), ("judge-readiness", "--probe-judges")):
423	        supervisor.start_task(
424	            label, [sys.executable, "-m", "open_instruct.miles.execution.cluster", str(path), option, str(root)], env
425	        )
426	    print(f"Startup branches launched; preparing Core workflow. Driver log: {root}/driver-{rank}.log", flush=True)
427	    supervisor.run_child("driver", [sys.executable, "-m", "open_instruct.miles", "train", str(path)], env)

430	def probe(root):
431	    with stage(SimpleNamespace(save=root / "ray-readiness"), "ray_cluster_readiness"):
432	        deadline = startup.deadline(root)
433	        ray = importlib.import_module("ray")
434	        ray.init(address=os.environ["RAY_ADDRESS"])
435	        expected = read(root / "expected-ray.json")
436	        try:
437	            while True:
438	                if time.time() >= deadline:
439	                    raise TimeoutError("Ray replicas did not join before the startup deadline")
440	                nodes = ray.nodes()
441	                if len([n for n in nodes if n.get("Alive")]) >= len(expected):
442	                    require_layout(nodes, expected)
443	                    break
444	                time.sleep(1)
445	            write(root / "ray-layout.json", {"expected": expected, "actual": nodes})
446	        finally:
447	            ray.shutdown()
448	        write(root / "ray-ready.json", {"ready_unix": time.time()})
449

451	def probe_judges(spec, root):
452	    timing_args = SimpleNamespace(save=root / "judge-readiness")
453	
454	    async def qualify():
455	        registry = judging.registry(spec.judges)
456	        paths = [
457	            root / f"judge-ready-{name}.json"
458	            for name, service in registry["judges"].items()
459	            if service["mode"] == "managed"
460	        ]
461	        with stage(timing_args, "judge_http_readiness"):
462	            while not all(path.is_file() for path in paths):
463	                await asyncio.sleep(1)
464	        if spec.judges["judging"]["bindings"]:
465	            with stage(timing_args, "judge_canaries"):
466	                await judge_registry.probe(root / "judge-canaries.json")
467	        write(root / "judges-ready.json", {"ready_unix": time.time()})
468	
469	    remaining = startup.deadline(root) - time.time()
470	    asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(qualify(), timeout=max(0, remaining)))

473	def main():
474	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
475	    parser.add_argument("config", type=Path)
476	    probes = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
477	    probes.add_argument("--probe", type=Path)
478	    probes.add_argument("--probe-judges", type=Path)
479	    args = parser.parse_args()

482	    elif args.probe_judges:

"""Manage the Ray cluster and fixed-weight judge services inside a Beaker allocation.
Each replica joins a fresh attempt directory on shared WEKA, starts its assigned
processes and reports readiness, completion or failure to its peers. Supervision
and heartbeats bound startup hangs and peer failures alongside Beaker's propagation
settings, while the leader runs the training workflow without Beaker credentials.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import contextlib
import importlib
import ipaddress
import json
import os
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from urllib import request

from open_instruct.miles.configuration import inference_profiles, topology, validation
from open_instruct.miles.configuration.run_spec import RunSpec
from open_instruct.miles.execution import rendezvous, startup
from open_instruct.miles.execution.timing import stage
from open_instruct.miles.infrastructure import gpu_hardware, infra_timeouts
from open_instruct.miles.rewards import judge_registry, judge_server, judging


def write(path, value):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = path.with_name(path.name + "." + uuid.uuid4().hex + ".tmp")
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, allow_nan=False))
    temporary.replace(path)


def read(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


def free_ports(count):
    """Select distinct local ports together, then release them for service startup.

    Holding every socket until selection finishes prevents duplicates within this
    batch. Other processes can still claim a port after these sockets close.
    """
    ports = []
    with contextlib.ExitStack() as sockets:
        for _ in range(count):
            stream = sockets.enter_context(socket.socket())
            stream.bind(("0.0.0.0", 0))
            ports.append(stream.getsockname()[1])
    return ports


def terminate(process):
    if process is None:
        return
    # Even a finished group leader may have surviving grandchildren.
    with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        process.wait(timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(15))
    with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    process.wait(timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(15))


def require_layout(nodes, expected):
    live = [node for node in nodes if node.get("Alive")]
    actual = {node["NodeManagerAddress"]: node.get("Resources", {}).get("GPU", 0) for node in live}
    if len(live) != len(actual) or actual != expected:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Ray ownership differs from planned per-node GPU pools: {actual} != {expected}")


class Supervisor:
    def __init__(self, spec, root, rank, count):
        self.spec, self.root, self.rank, self.count = spec, root, rank, count
        self.startup_timeout = infra_timeouts.seconds(spec.launch["coordination"]["startup_timeout"])
        # Rendezvous has established a fresh attempt. Rank zero publishes one
        # budget for all subsequent startup work, including inventory/launch.
        deadline = time.time() + self.startup_timeout
        if rank == 0:
            write(root / "startup.json", {"deadline_unix": deadline})
        while not (root / "startup.json").is_file():
            if time.time() >= deadline:
                raise TimeoutError("Replica zero did not publish the startup deadline")
            time.sleep(1)
        self.startup_deadline = startup.deadline(root)
        self.heartbeat_timeout = infra_timeouts.seconds(spec.launch["coordination"]["heartbeat_timeout"])
        self.heartbeat_warning_at = {}
        self.children = []
        self.startup_tasks = []
        self.pending_health = {}
        self.logs = []
        self.health = {}
        self.health_failures = {}
        self.peer_heartbeats = {}
        self.next_health = 0.0
        self.log_offsets = {}
        self.stopping = threading.Event()
        self.failed = None
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.heartbeat, daemon=True)

    def heartbeat(self):
        while not self.stopping.is_set():
            try:
                write(self.root / f"heartbeat-{self.rank}.json", {"time": time.time(), "rank": self.rank})
                self.check_peer_heartbeats()
                for _, process in self.children:
                    if not (self.root / "complete.json").exists() and process.poll() is not None:
                        raise RuntimeError(f"Managed process {process.args[:3]} exited with {process.returncode}")
                if not (self.root / "complete.json").exists() and time.monotonic() >= self.next_health:
                    self.probe_health()
                    self.next_health = time.monotonic() + (2 if self.pending_health else 10)
            except BaseException as error:
                self.failed = error
                return
            self.stopping.wait(2)

    def check_peer_heartbeats(self):
        now = time.time()
        for rank in range(self.count):
            # A missing directory entry during shared-filesystem publication is
            # not evidence that an already joined peer never rendezvoused.
            # Retain its last observed heartbeat, without extending its deadline.
            try:
                observed = read(self.root / f"heartbeat-{rank}.json")["time"]
            except FileNotFoundError:
                observed = self.peer_heartbeats.get(rank)
            else:
                self.peer_heartbeats[rank] = observed
            if observed is None:
                if now >= self.startup_deadline:
                    raise TimeoutError(f"Replica {rank} did not rendezvous")
            else:
                age = now - observed
                if age > min(
                    30, self.spec.launch["coordination"]["heartbeat_timeout"]
                ) and now >= self.heartbeat_warning_at.get(rank, 0):
                    infra_timeouts.logger.warning(
                        "Replica heartbeat stale: observer=%s replica=%s age_s=%.1f deadline_s=%s",
                        self.rank,
                        rank,
                        age,
                        self.heartbeat_timeout,
                    )
                    self.heartbeat_warning_at[rank] = now + 30
                if age > self.heartbeat_timeout:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"Replica {rank} heartbeat expired")

    def probe_health(self):
        # Judges load on their own GPUs while Ray and the workflow start. Only
        # promote a service into steady-state liveness checks once HTTP is ready.
        for name, url in tuple(self.pending_health.items()):
            try:
                with request.urlopen(url, timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(3)) as response:
                    if response.status != 200:
                        raise OSError(f"Judge HTTP status {response.status}")
            except OSError as error:
                if time.time() >= self.startup_deadline:
                    raise TimeoutError(f"Judge {name} did not become ready before the startup deadline") from error
                continue
            self.health[name] = url
            self.pending_health.pop(name)
            write(self.root / f"judge-ready-{name}.json", {"ready_unix": time.time()})
        for name, url in tuple(self.health.items()):
            try:
                with request.urlopen(url, timeout=infra_timeouts.seconds(5)) as response:
                    if response.status != 200:
                        raise RuntimeError("Unhealthy HTTP response")
                self.health_failures[name] = 0
            except (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
                self.health_failures[name] = self.health_failures.get(name, 0) + 1
                write(
                    self.root / f"judge-health-{self.rank}.json",
                    {"failures": self.health_failures, "error": str(error)},
                )
                if self.health_failures[name] >= 3:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"Judge {name}: three consecutive liveness failures") from error

    def relay_logs(self):
        for stream in self.logs:
            with Path(stream.name).open("rb") as reader:
                reader.seek(self.log_offsets.get(stream.name, 0))
                raw = reader.read(16384)
                self.log_offsets[stream.name] = reader.tell()
            if raw:
                print(f"[{Path(stream.name).name}] " + raw.decode(errors="replace"), end="", flush=True)

    def check(self):
        self.relay_logs()
        if self.failed:
            raise self.failed
        for label, process in self.startup_tasks:
            if process.poll() not in (None, 0):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Startup task {label} exited with {process.returncode}; see {self.root}")
        failures = list(self.root.glob("failed-*.json"))
        if failures:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Peer failure: {read(failures[0])}")

    def wait(self, predicate, *, timeout=None):
        # Explicit timeouts are for post-training completion, which must not
        # inherit an already expired startup deadline.
        deadline = self.startup_deadline if timeout is None else time.time() + infra_timeouts.seconds(timeout)
        started = time.monotonic()
        next_warning = started + 30
        while True:
            if time.monotonic() >= next_warning:
                infra_timeouts.logger.warning(
                    "Cluster readiness still waiting: replica=%s elapsed_s=%.1f remaining_s=%.1f",
                    self.rank,
                    time.monotonic() - started,
                    max(0, deadline - time.time()),
                )
                next_warning = time.monotonic() + 30
            self.check()
            result = predicate()
            if result:
                return result
            if time.time() >= deadline:
                raise TimeoutError("Cluster startup/readiness deadline expired")
            time.sleep(1)

    def start(self, label, command, env, *, monitor=True):
        log = (self.root / f"{label}-{self.rank}.log").open("w")
        self.logs.append(log)
        process = subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True)
        try:
            write(self.root / f"process-{label}-{self.rank}.json", {"started_unix": time.time(), "pid": process.pid})
        except BaseException:
            terminate(process)
            raise
        if monitor:
            self.children.append((label, process))
        return process

    def start_task(self, label, command, env):
        """Own a finite startup subprocess without treating success as a crash."""
        process = self.start(label, command, env, monitor=False)
        self.startup_tasks.append((label, process))
        return process

    def run_child(self, label, command, env):
        process = self.start(label, command, env, monitor=False)
        try:
            while process.poll() is None:
                self.check()
                time.sleep(1)
            if process.returncode:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"{label} exited with {process.returncode}; see {self.root}/{label}-{self.rank}.log"
                )
        finally:
            terminate(process)

    def close(self):
        self.stopping.set()
        self.thread.join(timeout=5)
        for _, process in reversed(self.children + self.startup_tasks):
            terminate(process)
        for stream in self.logs:
            stream.close()


def run(path):
    spec = RunSpec.load(path)
    ray_cpus = validation.ray_cpus(os.environ)
    compiled = spec.compile()
    layout = topology.plan(spec, compiled)
    if (Path(spec.output["root"]) / "workflow.json").exists() and not spec.launch["auto_resume"]:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "This run directory already has a workflow; choose a new output.root before starting services"
        )
    rank = int(os.environ.get("OI_MILES_REPLICA_RANK", os.environ.get("BEAKER_REPLICA_RANK", "0")))
    count = int(os.environ.get("OI_MILES_REPLICA_COUNT", os.environ.get("BEAKER_REPLICA_COUNT", "1")))
    if count != layout["replicas"] or rank not in range(count):
        raise RuntimeError("Beaker replica topology differs from the submitted run")
    attempt = os.environ["OI_MILES_LAUNCH_ID"]
    root = rendezvous.join(
        Path(spec.output["root"]) / "cluster" / attempt,
        rank,
        count,

    )
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    address = socket.gethostbyname(os.environ.get("BEAKER_NODE_HOSTNAME", socket.gethostname()))
    supervisor = Supervisor(spec, root, rank, count)

    def interrupt(signum, frame):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Replica received signal {signum}")

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, interrupt)
    supervisor.thread.start()
    try:
        write(root / f"node-{rank}.json", {"address": address, "rank": rank})
        paths = [root / f"node-{index}.json" for index in range(count)]
        supervisor.wait(lambda: all(p.is_file() for p in paths))
        assignments = topology.assign(layout, [read(p)["address"] for p in paths])
        node = assignments[address]
        print(f"Replica {rank} address={address} assignment={node}; reports={root}", flush=True)
        head = min(assignments, key=ipaddress.IPv4Address)
        inventory = gpu_hardware.inventory()
        visible = [device["id"] for device in inventory]
        if len(visible) != layout["gpus_per_replica"]:
            raise RuntimeError("Visible devices differ from the Beaker GPU allocation")
        ray_devices, judges = topology.devices(node, visible)
        inventory_report = gpu_hardware.rollout_inventory(node, inventory)
        profile = compiled.inference_profile
        if node["rollout_gpus"]:
            inference_profiles.validate_hardware(profile, inventory_report["hardware"])
        write(root / f"inference-profile-{rank}.json", {"profile": profile, "address": address, **inventory_report})
        # Three Ray agent ports everywhere; the head needs three more Ray ports.
        ports = iter(free_ports(len(judges) + (6 if address == head else 3)))
        write(
            root / f"placement-{rank}.json",
            {
                "address": address,
                "head": head,
                "ray_devices": ray_devices,
                "judge_devices": judges,
                "layout": layout,
                "ray_cpus": ray_cpus,
            },
        )
        env = dict(os.environ)
        registry = judging.registry(spec.judges)
        for name, devices in judges.items():
            service = registry["judges"][name]
            port = next(ports)
            service["endpoint"] = f"http://{address}:{port}/v1"
            command = judge_server.command(service, port)
            judge_env = dict(env, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=",".join(devices))
            # The fixed judge is a standard Qwen model, not an Olmo extension.
            judge_env.pop("SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE", None)

        env["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = ",".join(ray_devices)
        env["RAY_NODE_IP_ADDRESS"] = address
        if address == head:
            port = next(ports)
            write(root / "head.json", {"address": f"{head}:{port}"})
        supervisor.wait(lambda: (root / "head.json").exists())

            "ray",
            "start",
            "--block",
            "--node-ip-address",

            str(ray_cpus),
            "--disable-usage-stats",

        ray_command += [

def start_workflow(path, supervisor, env, assignments, registry):
    """Start preparation immediately, with separate Ray and judge readiness gates."""
    root, rank = supervisor.root, supervisor.rank
    # Endpoint discovery is complete; readiness is deliberately separate.
    # The driver can prepare model/data while Ray and judges initialize.
    write(root / "expected-ray.json", {ip: n["ray_gpus"] for ip, n in assignments.items()})
    write(root / "registry.json", registry)
    env[startup.REPORT_DIR_ENV] = str(root)
    for label, option in (("ray-readiness", "--probe"), ("judge-readiness", "--probe-judges")):
        supervisor.start_task(
            label, [sys.executable, "-m", "open_instruct.miles.execution.cluster", str(path), option, str(root)], env
        )
    print(f"Startup branches launched; preparing Core workflow. Driver log: {root}/driver-{rank}.log", flush=True)
    supervisor.run_child("driver", [sys.executable, "-m", "open_instruct.miles", "train", str(path)], env)


def probe(root):
    with stage(SimpleNamespace(save=root / "ray-readiness"), "ray_cluster_readiness"):
        deadline = startup.deadline(root)
        ray = importlib.import_module("ray")
        ray.init(address=os.environ["RAY_ADDRESS"])
        expected = read(root / "expected-ray.json")
        try:
            while True:
                if time.time() >= deadline:
                    raise TimeoutError("Ray replicas did not join before the startup deadline")
                nodes = ray.nodes()
                if len([n for n in nodes if n.get("Alive")]) >= len(expected):
                    require_layout(nodes, expected)
                    break
                time.sleep(1)
            write(root / "ray-layout.json", {"expected": expected, "actual": nodes})
        finally:
            ray.shutdown()
        write(root / "ray-ready.json", {"ready_unix": time.time()})


def probe_judges(spec, root):
    timing_args = SimpleNamespace(save=root / "judge-readiness")

    async def qualify():
        registry = judging.registry(spec.judges)
        paths = [
            root / f"judge-ready-{name}.json"
            for name, service in registry["judges"].items()
            if service["mode"] == "managed"
        ]
        with stage(timing_args, "judge_http_readiness"):
            while not all(path.is_file() for path in paths):
                await asyncio.sleep(1)
        if spec.judges["judging"]["bindings"]:
            with stage(timing_args, "judge_canaries"):
                await judge_registry.probe(root / "judge-canaries.json")
        write(root / "judges-ready.json", {"ready_unix": time.time()})

    remaining = startup.deadline(root) - time.time()
    asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(qualify(), timeout=max(0, remaining)))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("config", type=Path)
    probes = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    probes.add_argument("--probe", type=Path)
    probes.add_argument("--probe-judges", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.probe:
        probe(args.probe)
    elif args.probe_judges:
        probe_judges(RunSpec.load(args.config), args.probe_judges)
    else:
        run(args.config)

    main()

"""Epoch budgets must reach native MILES without a default rollout override."""

import copy

import pytest

from open_instruct.miles.configuration import run_spec


def test_num_epoch_uses_native_budget_instead_of_the_default_rollout_limit(tmp_path):
    document = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "name": "epochs",
        "model": {"source": "model"},
        "output": {"root": str(tmp_path)},
        "data": {"tasks": [{"task": "gsm8k", "train_count": 32, "eval_count": 8}]},
        "training": {"num_epoch": 2},
    }
    spec = run_spec.RunSpec.from_dict(document, config_path=tmp_path / "run.toml")
    compiled = spec.compile()
    assert compiled.miles["num_epoch"] == 2 and "num_rollout" not in compiled.miles
    assert "--num-epoch" in compiled.arguments() and "--num-rollout" not in compiled.arguments()
    assert compiled.core.save_final_checkpoint
    assert "save_interval" not in compiled.miles
    spec.plan()  # Includes warnings/checkpoint planning before dataset size is known.
    for section in ("training", "miles"):
        conflicting = copy.deepcopy(document)
        conflicting.setdefault(section, {})["num_rollouts" if section == "training" else "num_rollout"] = 7
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Choose num_epoch or num_rollouts"):
            run_spec.RunSpec.from_dict(conflicting).compile()
    document["training"]["save_checkpoints"] = False
    assert not run_spec.RunSpec.from_dict(document).compile().core.save_final_checkpoint
    for count in (0, -1, True):
        document["training"]["num_epoch"] = count
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="num_epoch"):
            run_spec.RunSpec.from_dict(document).compile()

content.thinking:
The diff is very clear now. Changes relevant to this lecture (u8-l3):

1. **workflow.py** (`execute` completion check): previously compared `completed[-1] + 1 == config.miles.get("num_rollout")`; now `== result.get("num_rollout", config.miles.get("num_rollout"))` — driver result takes precedence. This matters for epoch budget runs where native MILES resolves `num_rollout` after loading data, so the compiled config has no `num_rollout`.

2. **driver.py**: 
   - Return dict now includes `"num_rollout": args.num_rollout`.
   - Save condition adds `save_final_checkpoint and rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1` — the final checkpoint is saved at the last rollout even without a periodic save_interval.

3. **run_spec.py**:

allocations and batch geometry.

source read-only and give each run a new output directory. The colocated example

runs before training in the pinned runtime. Neither proves memory fit or learning
quality.

Use `train` inside an allocation. `run` launches the config-driven Beaker
workflow and `status` inspects the submitted run:

```bash

python -m open_instruct.miles status runs/my-run.toml
```

See the complete [laptop and Beaker-session launch guide](launching.md).

working tree and set `MILES_BASE_IMAGE` to the locally loaded base image recorded

host needs the Beaker CLI and credentials, plus Docker when building.

allocations with independent trainer, rollout and named-judge GPU counts.

`~/.cache/open-instruct/miles/launches` by default; set `MILES_LAUNCH_RECEIPTS`

`complete` or `failed`; logs and small JSON reports are also collected into

output root requires an unchanged run specification; completed runs cannot be overwritten. With `auto_resume=true`,
a retry adopts verified preparation and loads the latest completed Core

from the initial model again. A killed process may leave the last recorded

launching. See the [scheduling contract](launching.md#distributed-scheduling-contract)
for GPU placement, protected runtime and the separate CPU-job rules.

```bash

  --set 'tracking.wandb_group="gsm8k-parity-check"'
```

variable substitution. If structured names and native escape-hatch names
address the same resolved option, different values are rejected rather than silently choosing a winner.

controls must be finite. Zero-temperature evaluation and zero auxiliary-loss
coefficients remain valid.

mounted data and tokenizer are available. Paths are not required to exist on

subclass. These checks do not replace the pinned runtime's full validation or
prove that a model fits the selected GPUs.

values. `plan` shows how structured aliases resolve into Core and native MILES options.

79	workflow state; consult the Beaker attempt status when checking liveness.
80	
81	Review the copied run's scheduling settings and rendered Beaker spec before
82	launching. See the [scheduling contract](launching.md#distributed-scheduling-contract)
83	for GPU placement, protected runtime and the separate CPU-job rules.
84	
85	All commands accept repeatable TOML overrides, for example:
86	
87	```bash
88	python -m open_instruct.miles plan configs/miles/examples/dev.toml \
89	  --set training.num_rollouts=20 \
90	  --set 'tracking.wandb_group="gsm8k-parity-check"'
91	```
92	
93	Strings require TOML quotes inside shell quotes. There is no implicit environment
94	variable substitution. If structured names and native escape-hatch names
95	address the same resolved option, different values are rejected rather than silently choosing a winner.
96	
97	## Input errors and debugging
98	
99	`plan` checks field names, scalar types, common numeric ranges and batch/GPU
100	geometry on CPU. The same checks run before `run` builds an image. Unknown
101	fields suggest a nearby spelling where possible; structured aliases retain
102	context such as `optimizer.learning_rate` when reporting a native-option error.
103	Booleans must be unquoted `true`/`false`, counts must be integers, and numeric
104	controls must be finite. Zero-temperature evaluation and zero auxiliary-loss
105	coefficients remain valid.
106	
107	Expected input failures print an actionable error and exit with status 2.
108	Malformed JSONL reports the source file and line; invalid prepared rows report
109	the partition and row. These file checks happen during preparation, where the
110	mounted data and tokenizer are available. Paths are not required to exist on
111	the submitting host.
112	
113	Use `--debug` on any command to include the traceback for an input error:
114	
115	```bash
116	python -m open_instruct.miles validate run.toml --debug
117	```
118	
119	Unexpected runtime failures still retain their tracebacks by default. Python
120	callers can catch `open_instruct.miles.errors.InputError`, a `ValueError`
121	subclass. These checks do not replace the pinned runtime's full validation or
122	prove that a model fits the selected GPUs.
123	
124	## Configuration sections
125	
126	Use [which section to edit](configuration.md#which-section-to-edit) for the
127	section map and [workflow fields](configuration.md#workflow-fields) for accepted
128	values. `plan` shows how structured aliases resolve into Core and native MILES options.
129	
130	Data preparation uses open-instruct's task and reward machinery. A familiar
131	section name does not imply that every Megatron-implementation catalog entry or external
132	service is available. Named recipe selection is rejected; express the supported
133	task mix with `[[data.tasks]]` or adopt an immutable manifest. Reusing an immutable prepared manifest is the most direct
134	way to keep prompts, splits, rendering and reward configuration fixed between
135	runs. Compare the recorded question IDs when checking parity; matching counts
136	alone does not establish identical datasets.
137	
138	## Collection and policy settings
139	
140	A collection contains `rollout_batch_size × n_samples_per_prompt` responses;
141	`global_batch_size` determines responses per optimizer update. Their ratio is
142	the number of updates per collection. See the
143	[generated recipe tables](configuration.md#example-recipes) for each starter and
144	[policy lag and TIS](async-pipeline.md#policy-lag-and-tis) when changing that ratio.
145	Router replay, auxiliary losses and reference KL are independent settings.
146	
147	## Trainer mappings that need care
148	
149	Most optimizer, sampling and SGLang names carry through directly. These trainer
150	settings have a narrower meaning here:
151	
152	| Megatron concept | Core meaning or limitation |
153	| --- | --- |
154	| `trainer.gpus`, `trainer_num_nodes`, `expert_parallel_size` | `trainer.gpus` is GPUs per trainer node; total trainer GPUs are `gpus × trainer_num_nodes`. `expert_parallel_size` sets the expert process group. Consult the [topology guide](topology.md) for supported placement and limits. |
155	| `activation_recompute` | Core activation checkpointing; it does not promise the same recomputation granularity as Megatron. |
156	| `micro_batch_size` | Core microbatch size is one. Optional document-isolated packing combines samples within an optimizer partition; see [packing](sequence-packing.md). |
157	| `trainer_flash_attention_version=4` | Core `flash_4`; before loading the policy, the submitted job's attention preflight compares its forward and backward pass with a reference on the allocated GPU. |
158	| `trainer_backend="optimized"` | No equivalent preset: use explicit Core attention, row-specialization and other supported controls. |
159	| Trainer offload during colocation | Core stays resident. Full-model Megatron colocation memory fractions cannot be copied safely. |
160	| `async_save` | Unsupported; native Core saves are synchronous. Final HF export is a separate post-training operation. |
161	| Megatron conversion/layout settings | Do not apply to Core. The HF descriptor and native Core checkpoint have distinct roles. |
162

164	[admission guidance](throughput-profiles.md#size-engine-admission-from-memory).

"""Record how long the driver spends awaiting each stage of a training run.
The JSONL timeline includes stage identity, rollout number and success or failure,
allowing offline tools to separate initialization, generation wait, training and
publication costs. For asynchronous runs these are driver wait times, so generation
work that overlaps training is not counted again as generation wait.
"""

import json
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

from open_instruct.miles.infrastructure import infra_timeouts


@contextmanager
def stage(args, name, rollout_id=None, *, details=None):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    wall = time.time()
    passed = False
    try:
        with infra_timeouts.watch(f"driver stage={name} rollout={rollout_id}"):
            yield
        passed = True
    finally:
        if getattr(args, "save", None):
            root = Path(args.save)
            root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with (root / "driver_timing.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
                stream.write(
                    json.dumps(
                        dict(
                            stage=name,
                            rollout_id=rollout_id,
                            started_unix=wall,
                            seconds=time.perf_counter() - started,
                            passed=passed,
                            **({"details": details} if details is not None else {}),
                        )
                    )
                    + "\n"
                )


def evaluation_stage(args, rollout_id, *, initial=False):
    """Shared-engine dispatch awaits eval; snapshot dispatch only submits work."""
    snapshots = getattr(args, "eval_uses_snapshots", False)
    keys = (
        "rollout_num_gpus",
        "rollout_num_gpus_per_engine",
        "sglang_server_concurrency",
        "sglang_max_running_requests",
        "sglang_max_total_tokens",
        "sglang_max_mamba_cache_size",
        "sglang_cuda_graph_max_bs_decode",
        "sglang_mem_fraction_static",
        "sglang_context_length",
        "sglang_disable_radix_cache",
    )
    return stage(
        args,
        "evaluation_dispatch" if snapshots else "evaluation",
        rollout_id,
        details={
            "phase": "initial" if initial else "periodic",
            "scope": "snapshot_submission" if snapshots else "blocking_shared_engine_evaluation",
            "configured_serving": {key: getattr(args, key, None) for key in keys},
        },
    )
